subject: Site telemetry consent migration plan and DPA questions
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightretail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry consent for site migration

Hi Priyom,

We're starting a migration of our marketing tag stack later this quarter and want to confirm a couple of privacy items for Redwood-hosted telemetry coming from our web console. High-level ask: will the telemetry/usage pings and marketing analytics you collect be covered under the standard DPA terms and what subprocessors are involved for cross-border storage/processing?

Specifically:
- Where is customer telemetry stored (regions)?
- If we use your streaming debug console feature, does that persist any raw PII from the browser?
- Can we get a current list of subprocessors and whether any of them are located outside the EEA?

We're also mapping cookie categories to telemetry events (I can share our sheet). Legal would like to confirm retention windows and whether we can configure per-account retention for BrightRetail.

Thanks — happy to take a 30m call if that's easier.

Best,
Alex
Alex Turner
Director, Product Analytics
BrightRetail Inc.
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry consent for site migration

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Hannah from Privacy/Trust for the DPA/subprocessor specifics.

Quick answers up front:
- Redwood stores telemetry in regional buckets by default; for BrightRetail we can pin to eu-west-1.
- Streaming console: we do not persist browser-level PII by default; KV traces include request metadata and anonymized IP by hashing/truncation.
- Subprocessor list: Hannah will share the most recent inventory and indicate where cross-border transfers occur.

If you can drop the cookie/event mapping sheet, Hannah will annotate the telemetry types that are covered by our standard DPA vs. ones that require a narrow addendum. I'm available for a call next week.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Sales, Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightretail.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry consent for site migration

Alex — thanks, I pulled together the initial checklist while Priyom and Marissa coordinate the MAP. A few clarifying questions to align legal and engineering: 

1) Event classification: are you sending any raw user identifiers (email, customer_id, external_id) as attributes on pageview or only as hashed IDs? If raw identifiers are sent we need contract language around PII processing and can propose a minimal addendum.

2) Retention: you mentioned per-account retention. We can support configurable retention policies but need to confirm the shortest required period for marketing analytics (our default is 90 days for web events; logs for debugging are 30 days). Do you need >90 days for historical attribution?

3) Consent gating: does BrightRetail plan to gate telemetry at the tag-manager/consent-layer (i.e., block calls until user opts in) or do you plan to send and filter server-side? We recommend client-side gating for marketing cookies to avoid transfer of opt-out data.

4) Cross-border transfers: please confirm whether your organization needs all processing to remain in the EEA. If so, we can provide EU-only processing and provide a signed DPA addendum listing EU-based subprocessors. If not, we'll list which subprocessors may be US-based (analytics vendor for batch processing, logging infra).

I attached a quick cookie-event mapping template (telemetry-cookie-mapping.xlsx) with notes — please populate column B with the exact event names you plan to send.

Hannah Schmitt
Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightretail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com, legal@brightretail.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry consent for site migration

Thanks Hannah — attaching our initial mapping and the product team's notes. Quick answers inline:

- Identifiers: we will send customer_id and hashed_email for analytics; no cleartext emails in pageview events. We will send full customer_id in account-level server calls for attribution.
- Retention: marketing needs 13 months for attribution reporting; can you support per-account retention = 395 days?
- Consent gating: we plan to block marketing tags until opt-in, but keep functional telemetry (session, error reporting) enabled.
- EU-only: ideally yes — BrightRetail's legal prefers EU-only processing for telemetry. If Redwood can provide EU-only subprocessors and confirm no US-hosted backups, that would be a requirement for us.

I also attached BR-DataProcessingAddendum.pdf with the clauses our legal team typically requires. Let me know if you'd prefer a call to walk through the DPA items.

—Alex
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@brightretail.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry consent for site migration

Alex — thanks for the detailed responses and attachments. Next steps from Redwood: 

- Hannah will produce an EU-only subprocessor commitment and a marked-up DPA addendum where we can. Expect a draft within 3 business days.
- Engineering will confirm retention config for BrightRetail and whether we can support 395 days as a per-account retention option (initial estimate: yes, with tiered storage costs). Karh will take the lead here.
- Priyom/Marissa to share a one-page Mutual Action Plan (attached: MAP_BrightRetail_v1.docx) with milestones (DPA sign, infra pin, tag rollout, go/no-go).

Would you like to set a 30-min sync tomorrow to finalize the MAP? If so propose a time and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
